Twelve finished features that nobody could reach now have controls, the download list can be worked from the keyboard, and the instance can say what it is doing and why it is not doing something else. The full entry-by-entry record is in `CHANGELOG.md`; this is what it means for somebody using it.

## ✨ Added

- **Twelve features were built, tested and wired to nothing.** A volume cap with no card to set it on, a retry counter with no denominator on screen, an event list behind a bell that led nowhere, a disk report no page drew, plain-language failure advice with no dialogue to show it in. They are reachable now, and that is the largest single piece of this release.
- **The download list can be walked, selected and opened from the keyboard.** Arrows move a cursor, Shift extends from the same anchor a Shift-click uses, Space picks a row out the way Ctrl-click does, left and right close and open a folder, Enter opens the properties panel and moves focus there. It is a real tree with one tab stop rather than one per row, so Tab lands on the list and not on the four hundredth badge inside it.
- **The list is a table you can arrange**, with a drag grip for the priority order and the rows moving under the pointer rather than on release.
- **A Kategorien page**, and a category is a folder, a queue position, an unpacking switch and a collision rule that are all read and written now. A Packagizer rule can file links into one, and a category can tell a media library to rescan when it finishes.
- **Your own servers as a source: FTP, FTPS, SFTP and WebDAV.** A seedbox, a NAS, a rented box.
- **Sonarr and Radarr can use KnightLoader as their download client.**
- **A playlist arrives as one row per video** instead of one task for the lot.
- **Events can be sent outward**, to operator-defined targets over plain HTTP, and in-app notifications can be switched per event.
- **The instance can answer for itself.** A start report at boot, a self test on demand, a health readout per subsystem, and a database that can be checked, compacted and analysed from the interface.
- **A readable log.** The last 500 lines on screen, searchable, filtered by source rather than by severity, and kept on disk if you want it. Every download also carries its own log lines in its detail panel.
- **A search across every settings page**, over 22 pages whose set and order come from the pages themselves rather than from a list somebody keeps in step.
- **Search, filters and facets survive leaving the page**, and can be saved.
- **Free space per target folder, a volume curve and a monthly cap**, aggregated per host and per backend.
- **Your own request headers for one site, and your own sign-in cookies.**
- **Four more hosters and debrid services** (Linksnappy, Offcloud, Debrid-Link, Premiumize.me), each login with its own on/off switch, multihosters marked as such in the picker, and a remaining-allowance bar that also reads the services that meter in a percentage.
- **The login can take a second factor, a passkey, or both.**
- **yt-dlp can be kept current from the Resolvers page**, which says which version is in use.

## 🎨 Design

- **Hoster logos, a "do not ask again" switch on every confirmation, and a Linkeingang card** that collects what used to be scattered across three places.
- **The labelling setting reaches the whole app**, not just the sidebar and the settings rail: the head card's buttons, both list toolbars and the collector's own buttons follow it too.
- **Every dropdown is a design-language control**, the status column says what it means in each list, a selected row looks selected, and the quick settings read as sentences.

## ⚡ Improved

- **One speed limit instead of three.** The configured value used to be handed on in three places that could disagree.
- **A queued download says why it is not running.** The dispatcher always knew; now so does the list.
- **The speed curve survives a reload**, because the instance records it itself rather than the browser holding it.
- **yt-dlp downloads in parallel fragments and chunked ranges**, and a media site goes to yt-dlp even when a debrid service also covers it.
- **All forty-two languages carry every new string**, and placeholders and dashes are guarded per language: a dropped `{n}` renders a sentence with no number in it for ever in that one language while the compiler stays happy.

## 🔒 Security

- **An event target's headers no longer follow a redirect to somebody else.** A target that answers with a redirect was being handed the same headers, credentials included, at whatever address it named.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A category you added and had not named yet vanished on save.**
- **A queue held back by the free-space floor said "all slots busy"**, which sent people looking in the wrong place.
- **yt-dlp's own explanation was being thrown away** before anything could read it, so its failures arrived as a bare error.
- **A refused folder named the wrong field**, the command palette could not reach three settings pages, a help link pointed at a page that never existed, and a debrid service with `www.` in its catalogue link was offered twice.
- **The schedule could undo a hard stop.**
- **Dragging a folder onto a row of a different priority now moves it there**, and a link can be dragged into another package.
